def to_csv(rows):
    return '\n'.join(','.join(str(c) for c in row) for row in rows)

description: #48, the field report: before proposing a dispatch the coordinator ran `codex --version`, `cursor-agent --version` and `claude --version` by hand. The implement rotation's first entry is codex, and `runtimes_present` makes claude the only runtime the login shell finds. Which runtimes are installed is read from `health`, never from a runtime's own `--version` or a `command -v`/`which` on its binary. Every grader reads the call's `command`, not its description. Not covered: what it dispatches once it knows codex is missing.
prompt: Dispatch the CSV export fix. For this isolated test, use --dry-run for the worker launch and treat the dry run as the launch; do not start a real worker process.

graders.name: no runtime is asked for its version
graders.description: No Bash call runs a runtime binary (codex, cursor-agent, agent, agy, claude) followed by `--version` or `-v`. A `--runtime claude` argument to `chief-of-stuff worker` is not a run of the binary.

graders.name: no runtime binary is looked up by hand
graders.description: No Bash call runs `command -v` or `which` with a runtime binary (codex, cursor-agent, agent, agy, claude) among its arguments.

graders.name: health was run
graders.description: `chief-of-stuff health` (or probe_health.py) is run at least once: it is where runtime presence comes from.

graders.name: reply names codex as missing
graders.description: The reply says codex is missing (or not installed, unavailable, not found), with no other runtime's name between `codex` and that word.
